title: Streamlined correlation handoff proxy for multi-source log ingress
creator: Benji Chen
description:
Summary: Build a lightweight correlation handoff proxy in the ingest path that canonicalizes and surfaces a stable handoff_id across HTTP/gRPC/Kafka/worker boundaries so downstream aggregators (Loki/ELK) and tracing hooks can reliably join events without relying on brittle ad-hoc headers.

Goals:
- Generate and propagate a stable handoff_id at the first trusted ingress point when no canonical correlation id exists.
- Normalize incoming correlation formats (X-Request-ID, traceparent, custom tenant ids) into a single canonical field 'handoff_id' and a secondary 'source_ids' array for fidelity.
- Ensure the proxy emits structured envelope metadata expected by downstream pipelines: handoff_id, trace_id, original_headers, ingress_timestamp, tenant_id.
- Support translations between transports: HTTP headers -> Kafka message header -> gRPC metadata -> Worker queue attributes.
- Provide a safe rollout path behind a feature flag with opt-in sampling and a full backfill mode for historical events.

Non-goals: full rework of existing log schema, replacing trace context extraction libraries in services, or requiring all producers to change immediately.

Approach: implement proxy as an ingress service sitting in front of the existing log-forwarders and SDK shims. The proxy will:
- Inspect request/record for known correlation fields (X-Request-ID, traceparent, x-correlation-id, task_id).
- If none found or values inconsistent, generate a UUIDv7 handoff_id and attach it to the record.
- Canonicalize IDs and write to a single structured envelope field 'redwood.handoff' with keys: id, created_by, originals (comma-separated sources).
- Propagate the handoff_id forward via HTTP header, Kafka header 'redwood-handoff', gRPC metadata 'redwood-handoff', and SQS/worker attributes.
- Expose a real-time metric 'ingest.handoff.missing_rate' and 'ingest.handoff.duplicate_rate' and an error counter for invalid/malformed ids.

Backward compatibility: existing consumers will continue to receive original fields; the envelope is additive. The proxy supports a compatibility header 'redwood-handoff-legacy' to help older consumers opt-in.

Success metrics (first 6 weeks):
- handoff propagation coverage >= 95% for traffic routed through proxy.
- Reduction in orphaned-log traces (events with no correlating trace/span) by >= 40% in canary tenants.
- No more than 0.1% increase in ingest p95 latency at the proxy endpoint.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement proxy and unit/integration tests (local+k8s).
2) Internal canary: enable for internal infra and 2 low-traffic tenants at 5% sample.
3) Monitor metrics and dashboards for two weeks; iterate.
4) Expand to public tenants gradually (25% -> 60% -> 100%).
5) Run backfill job to annotate historical logs for a configurable retention window.

Monitoring & alerts: create dashboard tabs for coverage, missing_id_rate, duplicate_id_rate, schema-mismatch-count. Alert if missing_id_rate > 5% for more than 10 minutes or if proxy error rate > 0.5%.

Testing & QA: integration tests for cross-transport propagation, load test for 99th percentile added latency, fuzz tests for malformed headers.

Owner & contacts: Aisha Kapoor (owner), Benji Chen (designer), Observability-Eng on-call for pager routing.
comments: 2026-02-12: Initial RFC reviewed with Observability and Platform. Agreed on envelope format; decided on additive approach to avoid breaking consumers.
2026-02-20: Prototype implemented: local proxy adds redwood.handoff in HTTP and Kafka headers. Integration tests pass for basic propagation. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/418
2026-02-27: Design review notes: ensure traceparent extraction uses otel library; add metric for ‘original_ids_count’ to detect multiple conflicting ids. Action: Benji to update prototype.
2026-03-03: Load test (k6) at steady 2000 rps shows median add of 2.8ms and p95 add of 12ms. Meeting with runtime team to discuss edge optimizations (fast-path for already-canonicalized records).
2026-03-08: Security asked for HSM-backed UUID signing option for downstream verification — flagged for security review before GA. Ticket linked to security intake: SEC-341.
2026-03-10: Feature flag scaffolding merged. Canary rollout to internal infra scheduled for 2026-03-18. Next: finalize dashboards and update SDK docs.
